title: Stri: Gandhari's curse
hook: a blind king asks to embrace the man who killed his sons, and Krishna slides an iron statue into his arms

segments.voice: Your line: Stri: Gandhari's curse. Yesterday Vidura told the grieving king about a man in a well, still reaching for the honey. Did you taste the sweet thing you already had? Day eight hundred fifty-six.

A line of chariots and carts leaves Hastinapura, and behind it walk the women of the royal house, weeping, their hair unbound. They're going out to the battlefield to find their dead. At the front is Dhritarashtra, the blind old king, with Gandhari beside him. On the road, the Pandavas come to meet him: the five brothers who won, with Krishna. They bow. The king has to greet them. And he asks for one of them in particular. Today, an embrace that isn't what it seems.
screen: `THE WOMEN WALK OUT.` → `THE PANDAVAS COME TO MEET HIM.` → `HE ASKS FOR ONE.`

segments.voice: Dhritarashtra embraces Yudhishthira first, the text says, without joy. Then he asks for Bhima. Bhima is the one who killed Duryodhana and Duhshasana, the one who made the vows and kept them. Krishna understands what's in the old man's heart. So he quietly pushes Bhima aside and moves forward an iron statue of Bhima. Duryodhana had it made, in Ganguli's telling, to practice against with his mace. The blind king takes the iron figure in his arms, and he crushes it. He's so strong, and so full of grief and rage, that the statue breaks apart, and he hurts himself doing it. He falls to the ground, and Sanjaya lifts him up. And then Dhritarashtra weeps, crying out for Bhima, sure he has just killed him. Krishna speaks. It was not Bhima, he says, in effect. It was an image of iron. I knew what you meant to do. Your sons died because of their own deeds and because you didn't stop them. The king is ashamed, and maybe relieved. He washes, and then he embraces the brothers, Bhima too, with blessings this time. Look at the order of things here. A father's grief is so strong it could kill. Krishna doesn't shame him in front of everyone or refuse the embrace. He gives the grief something to break that isn't a person. And only after it breaks can the real embrace happen.
screen: `HE ASKS FOR BHIMA` · `AN IRON STATUE INSTEAD` · `THE STATUE IS CRUSHED` · then, large: `THEN THE REAL EMBRACE`

segments.voice: Sit with your arms resting loosely, hands in your lap. Make two fists, slowly, as tight as is comfortable. Breathe in and hold the grip. Breathe out and let the hands open. Do that a few times, then leave them open. Bring to mind someone you're angry with, and notice whether the hands want to close again. Let them stay open. If you pray, you can hold that person in your prayer with open hands. The bell holds the time.
Stri. In the book of the women, a blind king's grief breaks an iron Bhima, and only then can he embrace the living one.
Your line: only an image of iron. Today, if anger needs somewhere to go, give it a walk, a pillow, a page, before you meet the person. Tomorrow, Gandhari. Day eight hundred fifty-six.

howItsDone: The iron Bhima appears in retellings of the Stri Parva as a picture of a father's grief and of Krishna's foresight.

original.note: Dhritarashtra: the blind king, father of Duryodhana, who crushes the iron Bhima.

trapdoor: what you thought: the old king welcomed the victors after the war.
what it means: he meant to crush Bhima, and Krishna gave him an iron statue instead.
what a scholar hears: the statue Duryodhana made to practice his hatred becomes the thing that absorbs his father's, so the son's rage and the father's grief meet in iron.

notes: Audit pass: the cold embrace, the iron image made for Duryodhana's practice, Sanjaya raising the king, Krishna's reproof and the later embrace checked; no change needed.
All paraphrase; Krishna's words are a summary, not Ganguli's wording.

Confirm in Ganguli: the cold embrace of Yudhishthira; Krishna drags Bhima away and substitutes the iron image; the image was made by Duryodhana's order for practice; the king is injured, falls and is raised by Sanjaya; he weeps for Bhima; Krishna explains and reproves him; he washes and then embraces the brothers.
The meeting with Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma on the road (also in the Stri Parva) is left out.
